title: Church music and Buddy Bolden
summary: California old-timers like Ory and Bud Scott said the music came from church; Bolden supposedly took his music from the Baptist church.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Well, how important was the religious feeling in influencing all of this? Well, I think that's difficult to say, too.

Of course, for people like me that came down here years after it started, I would never know. But other people like, say, Kid Ori, for instance, and some of the first people I met in California, like Bud Scott, one of the old-timers, quite a few of those said that a lot of the music came right out of the churches of the jazz bands as if... I know it was either Ori or Bud Scott. I don't remember which one. It could have been Mutt Carey. I'm talking about Buddy Bolden. They said, well, he got all of his music right out of the Baptist church. He used to take his girlfriend whom he later married with, either Nora or Dora Bass. There were two twins. In fact, he took them both to church. He said he came out of that church and began swinging as if it were that simple. Of course, nothing could be quite that simple, but the churches always have had that wonderful beat in their music and a good melody and all going to... Maybe not so much harmony as we understand it, but they still have it. That church music has changed evidently very little, even compared to the jazz.
